items.problem: The field's consensus milestones remain collectively unmet: multimodality, reasoning, data, evaluation, cross-robot action generalization, efficiency, whole-body coordination, safety, agents, and coordination with humans.
items.notes: These are stated as the ten open challenges, i.e. milestones the field agrees are ahead, not a checklist any single system meets.

items.problem: Semantic-vs-embodied gap: VLA systems often understand the instruction but fail to execute the task, because they inherit LLM/VLM priors with no physical-interaction experience.
items.notes: A robustness/grounding problem, not a language problem; more language pretraining does not close it.

items.problem: Capability/robustness trade-off: an information-theoretic bound argues you cannot get both for free.
items.notes: If the bound holds, it reframes many "make it more capable" results as silently trading away robustness.

items.problem: Discrete action tokenization itself limits VLA scaling.
items.notes: A design-choice critique; continuous / diffusion action heads are the contender but not a settled replacement.

items.problem: Skill portability: commercial robot-skill marketplaces ship one-tap skills only as static playback. Open sub-problems are adaptation, cross-embodiment portability, provenance, safety verification, composition, and standardisation.
items.notes: Addressed directly by the sibling repo skillcrate-spec, which ships a format for provenance + adaptation + safety manifest + composition.

items.problem: Merging whole-body control with VLA policies (the HOVER / ASAP / OmniH2O line). One survey calls this the most important open problem in the field.

There is no SWE-bench for robotics: every paper uses a slightly different task suite, camera setup, and embodiment. The stated need is a small sharp benchmark plus a large contamination-controlled real-world one.
items.notes: The infrastructure half (contamination control, embodiment tagging, reproducible scorecards) is addressed by the sibling repo cleanbench-eval; the community benchmark itself remains open.

items.problem: Deformable-object manipulation lacks a universal high-DoF dexterous hand with tactile sensors and comprehensive evaluation at scale.
Learned simulators are now used as RL environments and even co-evolve with policies, but fidelity, long-horizon consistency, and trustworthy use as sim-to-real bridges remain open.
items.notes: Usable today; the open part is knowing WHEN to trust a rollout. The sibling repo trusthorizon-worldmodel measures long-horizon drift and rollout trust.

items.problem: Physics-sim limits: humanoid control tasks particularly highlight the simulation-to-reality gap, suggesting improved physics modeling is needed.
items.notes: Contact-rich and humanoid dynamics are where the gap is widest.

items.problem: Adversarial and backdoor attacks and environmental jailbreaks (malicious text/objects in the scene that steer the robot) have no robust defenses or evaluation standards yet.
items.notes: The evaluation-standard half is addressed by the sibling repo scenebreaker-vla (threat taxonomy, defenses, attack-success-rate scoring); robust guaranteed defenses remain open.

items.problem: Added abstractions increase complexity and steepen the learning curve, especially migrating from ROS 1; adoption is hindered by tooling immaturity, documentation gaps, and limited debugging support.

Open-problem table covers performance, real-time guarantees, scalability, security, and ecosystem maturity; few studies provide verified end-to-end guarantees under adversarial and multi-robot conditions.
Middleware fixes (hierarchical discovery, partition-based segmentation, RMW designs such as Zenoh) mitigate problems but increase ecosystem heterogeneity and interoperability complexity.

Misconfigurations, physical-unit mismatches, dependency bugs, and inter-component interaction bugs remain empirically common with only partial tooling; formal methods are hard to apply because building models and extracting parameters is manual.
items.notes: The cheap-to-detect classes are addressed by the sibling repo crosswire-lint (static + live cross-check for units, QoS/type, config, deps, service/action contracts); formal end-to-end proof stays open.

items.problem: Runtime verification and field-based testing of ROS systems is active but immature: no standard CI / hardware-in-the-loop practice.
Data acquisition at scale is unresolved and recurs across the 2026 surveys.
Reward design remains unresolved and recurs across the 2026 surveys.
Energy and compute budgets on-board recur as an unresolved constraint.
Human-intent prediction recurs as unresolved across the 2026 surveys.
